proof_steps: Bezout with both lines and adjunction classify all 17 negative curves.
Picard intersections and exact Schur complements characterize all negative-definite supports.
Pairwise disjoint cross-lines lie in a single grid row or column.
A finite binomial identity gives the seven coefficients; the chamber-support theorem identifies them with Zariski chambers.
claim_to_evidence.scope: The blow-up over C of six distinct plane points, precisely three on each of two distinct lines, with no marked point at their intersection.
unproved_limits: No classification of other ADE root types; no chamber volume formula; historical priority not independently settled.

correctness.rationale: For the two triple lines, Bezout bounds each of the two group multiplicity sums by plane degree. Adjunction then forces every nonexceptional negative curve other than the two special lines to be a cross-line. Thus there are precisely six exceptional (-1)-curves, nine cross-line (-1)-curves and two intersecting (-2)-curves. The negative-definite-support criterion yields Schur conditions r<=1, s<=1 or r+s<=1 for one/both roots. All pairwise disjoint cross-line selections are empty or contained in one grid row/column. The explicit binomial sum gives coefficients 1,17,100,281,401,255,37 and total 1092. An independent exact-rational matrix test enumerates all 131072 candidate supports, yielding identical counts.

value.rationale: Every coefficient is a canonical natural divisor-theoretic invariant of the specified family. The A2 chain is the first connected nontrivial exceptional root system on a cubic resolution, and simultaneous root supports are constrained differently from isolated-root configurations. Knowing the complete count by support size describes potential Zariski negative parts, stable-base-locus patterns, and quadratic pieces of the volume function. The invariant is not an arbitrary numerical slice or a mere repeat of the smooth case.
